name: United Kingdom
tagline: Offers in IB points before your results, and overseas fees since Brexit
summary: The UK runs one central application system, UCAS, for almost every undergraduate course in the country. You pick five courses, write one personal statement for all of them, and universities make conditional offers in IB points, usually something like '36 points overall including HL 6,6,5'. Since Brexit you are treated as an international student: you pay overseas tuition, you need a Student visa, and you cannot borrow from the UK student loan system. The money is the problem.
whyConsider: One application covers up to five courses across the whole country
Offers are made in IB points and HL grades, so you know exactly what you are aiming for
Everything is taught in English, and degrees in England and Wales take three years, like Denmark’s
Very deep subject specialisation from day one, and strong course-level reputations far beyond Oxbridge
Scotland's four-year degrees let you keep two or three subjects open before you specialise
Conditional offers in IB points solve the July problem outright: the whole process is designed around results that have not arrived yet.
One application, five choices, one personal statement, one reference — for almost every undergraduate course in the country.
Three-year bachelor degrees in England, Wales and Northern Ireland, so the total cost of a degree is less lopsided against the annual fee than it first looks.
watchOuts: Most EU students pay international tuition (in England, Irish citizens and settled-status holders can be exceptions). At Glasgow that is GBP 28,275-38,670 for 2027/28, and medicine is far higher

Most EU citizens get no UK tuition fee or maintenance loans and must fund it themselves; Irish citizens long resident in the EEA can get tuition fee support in England for courses starting before 2028
The Graduate Route post-study work visa is 18 months, not 2 years, for applications made on or after 1 January 2027 - so 18 months by the time you graduate
The 15 October deadline for Oxford, Cambridge, medicine, dentistry and veterinary is a full three months before everyone else
Admissions tests (UCAT, LNAT, ESAT, TMUA, TARA) have registration deadlines in September, before the UCAS deadline itself
An EU citizen pays the international fee. There is no EU rate, no home-fee status and, for most students, no access to UK student loans. This is the thing that decides whether the UK is realistic.
Oxford, Cambridge, medicine, dentistry and veterinary medicine all close on 15 October 2026 — more than a year before the course starts, and before most students have thought about applying at all.
Admissions tests for those courses register earlier still, and the registration deadline is not the test date.
Scotland runs four-year degrees and a separate system; Wales and Northern Ireland differ again on fees and support. "The UK" is four systems sharing one application portal.

ibRecognition.minimumPoints: No national minimum. Offers are set course by course; the competitive research universities typically ask 34-39 points overall.
ibRecognition.subjectLevelRule: Offers are expressed as a total plus three Higher Level grades. The University of Glasgow states its Economics requirement as '36 (6,6,5)' plus 'HL English or Humanities and HL Mathematics (Analysis & Approaches)'. LSE publishes a range of '37 points overall (with three Higher level subjects at grades 6 6 6) to 39 points overall (with three Higher level subjects at grades 7 6 6)'. Named HL subjects are common, and quantitative courses increasingly require HL Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches specifically.
ibRecognition.gradeConversion: The UCAS Tariff scores each IB component separately; there is no single Tariff figure for the Diploma as a whole. IBO Certificate in Higher Level: H7 = 56, H6 = 48, H5 = 32, H4 = 24, H3 = 12, H2 and H1 = 0. IBO Certificate in Standard Level: S7 = 28, S6 = 24, S5 = 16, S4 = 12, S3 = 6, S2 and S1 = 0. IBO Certificate in Extended Essay and IBO Certificate in Theory of Knowledge each: A = 12, B = 10, C = 8, D = 6, E = 4. CAS carries no Tariff points because it is not accredited.
notes: Most selective universities ignore the Tariff for IB applicants and make offers directly in points and HL grades. The Tariff matters mainly for less selective courses and for Clearing.

UCAS states the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge certificates were accredited in their own right and are awarded Tariff points 'when the certificates have been taken individually' - check with the university how your core points are counted inside a full Diploma.
LSE warns that 'offers made may also change from year to year' depending on the strength of the applicant pool, so published requirements are guidelines, not guarantees.
The IB Diploma itself requires 24 points or more to be awarded; UCAS records this but attaches no Tariff points to the Diploma as a whole.

language.englishTaughtBachelors: Everything. All undergraduate teaching is in English.
language.englishProof: UK universities generally accept IB English A at a specified grade, and often IB English B HL, as proof of English. Exact accepted grades vary by university; check each course page. A Student visa also requires English at the level set out in the immigration rules, which your university confirms on your CAS.
notes: Scottish universities teach in English too; Gaelic is not needed.
Because requirements are set per university, confirm the exact IB English grade accepted on the course page rather than assuming.

feeContext.summary: Since Brexit most EU, EEA and Swiss citizens pay the international fee, set per university and subject (Glasgow 2027/28: GBP 28,275 arts, GBP 33,708 science). In England you pay the Home fee with settled or pre-settled status, or, for autumn 2027 (the last intake it covers), as an Irish citizen or a UK national living in the EEA or Switzerland since before 2021 who meets a 3-year residence test. Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland set their own rules.

sources.title: Glasgow charges EU students the international fee; 2027/28 international fees are GBP 28,275 (arts and social sciences) and GBP 33,708 (science, engineering, nursing, medical, veterinary and life sciences), with MBChB and BDS still TBC.

In England an EU/EEA/Swiss student pays the international fee unless they meet a Home fee category: settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme; or, for courses starting before 1 August 2028, the temporary categories for Irish citizens and for UK nationals and their family living in the EEA or Switzerland, each with a three-year residence test.

Glasgow charges EU students the international fee; 2027/28 international fees are GBP 28,275 (arts and social sciences) and GBP 33,708 (science, engineering, nursing, medical, veterinary and life sciences), with MBChB and BDS still TBC.

sectorLandscape.summary: Almost every UK undergraduate course, at almost every institution, is applied for through one portal — which makes the sector look more uniform than it is. Underneath sit universities of very different ages and purposes, specialist conservatoires and art schools, further education colleges teaching degrees under a university’s validation, and degree apprenticeships that are jobs first. And the UK is four education systems, not one: Scotland’s degrees are four years and its fee and qualification rules are its own.

routes.what: Three-year bachelor degrees in England, Wales and Northern Ireland, four in Scotland, and specialised from the first term — you apply to read a subject rather than to a college in general. That suits a student who already knows, and suits a student who does not rather less than the Scottish or Dutch alternatives.

A separate system inside the same portal. Four-year honours degrees with a broader first two years, closer to a liberal-arts structure, and distinct fee and funding rules. For a student who wants to keep options open a while longer, this is the UK route to look at.
Music, dance and drama, with their own application route (UCAS Conservatoires) and their own calendar. Admission is by audition, and grades matter far less than the audition does.
routes.note: Applied for separately from the main UCAS scheme. Not covered in detail on this site.

routes.what: A paid job with a degree attached, funded by the employer, with no tuition fee to the apprentice. Applied for through the employer rather than UCAS, on the employer’s timetable.
routes.note: Almost always restricted to UK residents, so rarely open to an applicant from Denmark.

The UCAS undergraduate application fee for the 2027 cycle is GBP 34.50 for up to five choices.

deadlines.label: UCAS applications open for 2027 entry
deadlines.notes: You can start filling in the application from this date.

deadlines.label: UCAT (medicine and dentistry) - account registration, bursary and access arrangements open
deadlines.notes: Published on UCAT's test dates page as "20 May 2026 (14:00 UK Time)". You create the account first; test booking opens a month later.

deadlines.label: UCAT (medicine and dentistry) - booking opens
deadlines.notes: Published on UCAT's test dates page as "23 June 2026 (14:00 UK Time)". The 2026 cycle is the one that feeds 2027 entry — UCAT's own home page says registration instructions for UCAT 2027 will be published later, and that cycle belongs to 2028 entry. Booking deadline and testing window are separate entries.

deadlines.label: UCAT (medicine and dentistry) - testing window
deadlines.notes: Published on UCAT's test dates page as a window beginning "13 July 2026" and ending "24 September 2026", which the page labels the "Last test day". Your sitting must fall inside this window, and the window closes eight days after the booking deadline, so a late booking leaves almost no choice of slot. Context, not a milestone: UCAT publishes results to universities in "Early November" with no day given — you get your own score on the day you test.

deadlines.label: UAT-UK admissions tests (ESAT, TMUA, TARA) - test booking for the October sitting
deadlines.notes: Published as "Test booking opens for October 2026" on 20 July 2026 3pm BST, closing 28 September 2026 6pm BST. The time is the closing time. Accounts for 2027 entry opened on 1 June 2026. Oxford and Cambridge applicants must use this October sitting apart from a few exceptions. Used for 2027 entry by Cambridge, Imperial, Oxford and UCL (ESAT); those four and LSE, Warwick and Durham (TMUA); and Oxford and UCL (TARA), per the test pages on esat-tmua.ac.uk.

steps: From May 2026 you create one UCAS account and fill in one application. You choose up to five courses; for medicine, dentistry and veterinary you may only choose four in that subject.
You write a personal statement. From 2026 entry UCAS changed it from one long essay to three separate questions, and the same statement goes to all five courses.
A teacher at your school writes one academic reference. Ask early - references take time.
Register separately for any admissions test your course needs (UCAT, LNAT, ESAT, TMUA or TARA). These registrations close in September, before the UCAS deadline.
Submit by 15 October 2026 if you are applying to Oxford, Cambridge, medicine, dentistry or veterinary; otherwise by 13 January 2027.
Universities reply with conditional offers stated in IB points and HL grades. Some courses interview between December and March.
You reply with one firm choice and one insurance choice, then your IB results in July are matched against the conditions automatically.
application.selectionNotes: Every course is selective and sets its own conditions - there is no open access. Selection is on predicted grades, the personal statement, the reference, and for some courses an admissions test and interview. Oxford and Cambridge interview most shortlisted applicants in December. The UCAS application fee for the 2027 cycle is GBP 34.50 for up to five choices (it was GBP 28.95 for 2026 entry).

tuitionEuEea.value: Most EU students pay the international rate. In England, settled or pre-settled status, or (for autumn 2027, the last intake) being Irish or a UK national long resident in the EEA, can mean Home fees. Scotland sets its own rules.

tuitionNonEu.value: University of Glasgow 2027/28: Arts and Social Sciences GBP 28,275; Science, Engineering, Nursing and Medical/Veterinary/Life Sciences GBP 33,708; Veterinary Medicine and Surgery GBP 38,670 (Medicine MBChB and Dentistry BDS listed as TBC). Glasgow 2026/27 for comparison: Arts and Social Sciences GBP 27,720; Science and Engineering GBP 33,210; Medicine MBChB GBP 62,730; Dentistry BDS GBP 58,500. Across the sector a realistic 2026/27 planning range for an IB student from Denmark paying international fees is roughly GBP 22,000-40,000 (about €25,600-46,500) a year for a normal degree, and GBP 45,000-70,000 (about €52,300-81,400) a year for clinical medicine, at the ECB rate of 24 September 2026.

costs.applicationFee: UCAS application fee: GBP 34.50 for up to five choices in the 2027 cycle (GBP 28.95 for 2026 entry).

livingCostMonthly.value: University of Edinburgh estimates GBP 1,546 per month for a single undergraduate living in Edinburgh. London is higher; the Home Office assumes GBP 1,529 per month in London and GBP 1,171 outside London for visa purposes.

notes: For contrast, a UK 'Home' student in England pays a capped fee of GBP 9,790 in 2026-27 and GBP 10,050 in 2027-28. Most EU students will not get that rate; the exceptions are under tuition above.
Scottish universities charge EU students the international rate; the pre-Brexit free-tuition arrangement in Scotland ended in 2021.
Visa costs on top of tuition: Student visa GBP 558 from outside the UK, plus the Immigration Health Surcharge at GBP 776 per year of your course (both as published on GOV.UK, September 2026).
Glasgow's 2027/28 medicine and dentistry fees were still marked TBC on 2026-09-24 - re-check before you commit to a clinical course.

funding: Without settled or pre-settled status, most EU citizens get no UK tuition fee or maintenance loans: assume you pay every year in full. Irish citizens (tuition fee support) and UK nationals (tuition and maintenance) long resident in the EEA are the exceptions in England, for courses starting before 1 January 2028; see the Department for Education's FAQ (educationhub.blog.gov.uk).

University-run international scholarships are the main realistic source. Almost every university runs merit awards for international undergraduates, usually a partial fee discount of a few thousand pounds; amounts and deadlines are set per university, so check each one.

funding.note: The UK is outside the EU/EEA, so a full degree there follows separate rules, with its own ties-to-Denmark form: check su.dk early.

funding: Some universities still run specific EU-transition or country scholarships; check each course page rather than assuming.
workRights: On a Student visa for a full-time degree at a university, you can work up to 20 hours a week in term time and full time in the holidays (Immigration Rules, Appendix Student, ST 26.1). Your exact limit is printed on your visa.
residency: Irish citizens need no visa (Common Travel Area). Everyone else needs a Student visa; EU citizenship gives no shortcut since Brexit. You can apply from outside the UK up to 6 months before your course starts; the fee is GBP 558 and you also pay the Immigration Health Surcharge of GBP 776 for each year of your course. You need a Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (CAS) from your university and you must show money for living costs: GBP 1,529 per month for up to 9 months in London, or GBP 1,171 per month outside London, held in your account for 28 consecutive days ending no more than 31 days before you apply. At degree level you can normally stay up to 5 years.
housing: Almost all UK universities guarantee a place in university accommodation to first-year international students who apply by the stated deadline, which is usually in the summer once you have firmly accepted an offer. This is much easier than the Netherlands or Denmark. Apply the moment your firm choice is confirmed.
healthcare: You pay the Immigration Health Surcharge of GBP 776 (about €900) per year as part of the visa application. That gives you access to the NHS on the same basis as a UK resident for the length of your visa. Register with a local GP when you arrive. An EHIC or the Danish yellow card does not replace this.

systems.name: UCAS

coverage.includes: Almost every undergraduate course at almost every UK university and college.
coverage.excludes: Music, dance and drama at conservatoires, which use UCAS Conservatoires; and degree apprenticeships, which go through the employer.

choiceRules.note: Five choices, unranked, and every one may make an offer. Only four may be medicine, dentistry or veterinary medicine. One personal statement is sent to all five, which is the constraint that shapes the whole application: it has to work for every course you name, so five unrelated subjects produce a statement that argues for none of them.

systems.identityRequirement: A UCAS Hub account, and an academic reference from the school before the application can be sent.
systems.decisionModel: Universities decide individually and mostly make conditional offers, expressed in IB points and usually naming Higher Level grades. Some courses add an admissions test or an interview. An application received by the equal consideration date is guaranteed to be looked at; one after it may still be considered against remaining places.
systems.replyModel: Hold one firm choice and one insurance choice, the insurance normally with a lower offer. When results arrive in July the firm choice is confirmed if its conditions are met, the insurance if not, and Clearing exists for anyone holding neither.

sources.title: For 2027 entry: applications open 12 May 2026, can be submitted from 1 September 2026, with equal consideration on 15 October 2026 for Oxford, Cambridge, medicine, dentistry and veterinary medicine, and 13 January 2027 for most other courses. Clearing opens 2 July 2027 and the final date is 23 September 2027.

contextNotes.topic: "Equal consideration" is not the same as a deadline
contextNotes.text:
UCAS does not call 13 January a deadline. It calls it the equal consideration date, and the difference matters in both directions. An application in by then is guaranteed to be looked at. One after it is not rejected automatically — universities may still consider it, against whatever places are left, and many do.

So a student who misses it has not lost the year, and a student who assumes that means it is flexible has misunderstood the competition. Late is worse, and for a popular course it is much worse. Treat it as a real deadline and know that it is not an absolute one.
contextNotes.attribution: UCAS’s own wording on its dates and deadlines page
contextNotes.whatThisIsNot: The 15 October date for Oxford, Cambridge and medicine behaves differently in practice: those courses fill from the applicants who met it, and applying afterwards is close to pointless.

sources.title: For 2027 entry: applications open 12 May 2026, can be submitted from 1 September 2026, with equal consideration on 15 October 2026 for Oxford, Cambridge, medicine, dentistry and veterinary medicine, and 13 January 2027 for most other courses. Clearing opens 2 July 2027 and the final date is 23 September 2027.

contextNotes.topic: The one system that expects you not to have your results
contextNotes.text:
Everywhere else in Europe, IB results arriving on 6 July is a problem to be worked around — with a results service, a documentation deadline months earlier, or a decision made on something other than results. The UK simply assumes it. Universities make conditional offers in IB points, you accept one firmly and one as insurance, and in July the offers resolve against the results.

For an IB student this is a genuine structural advantage and it is worth knowing, because the UK is usually discussed in terms of cost. The trade is real: the process fits the qualification, and since Brexit the price for an EU citizen is the international one.

additionalGuidance.title: More about studying here
additionalGuidance.text: UK admissions are built around the fact that applicants do not yet have their results. Universities make conditional offers expressed in IB points — "36 overall including 6,6,5 at Higher Level" — and confirm them in July when the results arrive. For an IB student that solves an awkward problem: you know the exact grades you need before you sit the exams. What it introduced instead is cost: since Brexit an EU citizen pays the international fee, and there is no EU rate to fall back on.
